title: Write-up skill: a one-page Executive Summary before the table of contents
story: The project write-up used to go straight from the cover to the contents and then the cost tables, so leaders met numbers before knowing what was built. It now puts a one-page Executive Summary first: what was built and why, the cost-and-time headline, and Table 1's three totals. The skill checks the finished file and reports the first pages in order.

checks.criterion: The report's first pages are the cover, then a one-page Executive Summary, then the contents, and the summary's table matches Table 1.
checks.steps: In a throw-away repository, run /generate-project-writeup with made-up answers (contributors, dates, day rate 650, traditional team 3 for 8 months). Open the .docx it puts in Downloads.
checks.expected: Page 1 is the cover; page 2 is Executive Summary with what was built and why, the cost-and-time headline pointing to the Financial Summary, and a three-row table; page 3 is the contents. The table's cells equal Table 1's, and the chat report names the pages in that order.
